claims.content: Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer, having won auction item(s), checks out by choosing which item(s) to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and finally selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer begins checkout for one or more won auction items.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has selected the item(s) to pay for, chosen a shipping method, and selected a payment type.
in_scope_actions: Choose which won item(s) to pay for
excluded_adjacent_actions: Payment authorization/processing beyond selecting a payment type
variant_dimensions: Which won item(s) are selected for payment

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has at least one won auction item for which payment is still outstanding (unpaid auction winnings).
The Customer has previously chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default method of payment.
The Customer's account is not locked or in a review status.
The Customer starts checkout by clicking the 'Winnings Alert' link, the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email, or the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button.
The Customer chooses which won auction item(s) to pay for by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item in the list of won items.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.
The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking one of three buttons: 'Check out with PayPal', 'Check out with Amazon', or 'Checkout Later'.
Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may choose to pay using PayPal instead of a credit card or Amazon Payments.

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may select 'Credit Card' as the payment method in the 'My New Payment Method' section and enter new billing address details (Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country) to complete the transaction.

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may choose to create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account' and entering Country (defaulted to United States), then choosing a payment method of either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card'.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may log in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page to complete payment, instead of creating a new account or using Amazon.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button or radio button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a DIV layer explaining that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours), but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires.

missing_aspects: The 7-day/168-hour non-payment enforcement (order cancellation to Hold, account lock/Review, account suspension) cannot be anchored to a main_flow step because main_flow currently has no payment-deadline check; main_flow must be extended with such a check before these exception branches can be specified.
The claim asserts an exit outcome ('deferred checkout; no payment is completed') which is not explicitly supported by the cited evidence cards.

claims.content: Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and provides a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid' for items where the transaction has been successfully completed.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Postconditions describe a completed external payment (return from PayPal/Amazon and Paid status), but the Main Flow ends at the Customer selecting a checkout option. The Goal's scope contract explicitly excludes payment authorization/processing beyond selecting a payment type, so the Main Flow does not include the steps necessary to reach the Thank You page or the Paid status. The postconditions are therefore not reachable from the Main Flow as written. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The main flow ends with the Customer selecting a checkout option (PayPal, Amazon, or Checkout Later), but the postconditions require that the Amazon/PayPal checkout process has been completed, that the Customer is returned to a Thank You page, and that Payment Status is updated to 'Paid'. No main-flow step performs or completes the external payment process or handles the return/confirmation. This is reinforced by the goal's scope contract, which explicitly excludes payment authorization/processing beyond selecting a payment type, so the postconditions describe a state the current main flow cannot reach.

inconsistency_hints: Main flow Step 5 lists 'Checkout Later' as one of the normal checkout options. The goal is to complete checkout and payment by selecting a payment type; choosing 'Checkout Later' defers payment and does not select a payment type, so the main flow contains a non-success branch that is inconsistent with the goal's success boundary. The exception flow also treats 'Checkout Later' as an exception, further showing it belongs outside the main flow.

Alternative flow claim 0 says 'Diverges from Step 5' but describes selecting PayPal via a radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section. The alternative flow's coverage state flags that this action may occur specifically on the My Account page rather than during checkout, which would make main_flow step 5 a logically unrelated attachment point for this branch.
